div.head: Ine 39
div.ab: LXXXIII. Gif hwa fare unalyfed from his hlaforde oððe on oðre scire hine bestele, ⁊ hine mon geaxie, fare þær he wæs ær ond gesylle his hlaforde LX scll'.
LXXXIII. Gif hwa fare unaliefed fram his hlaforde oððe on oðre scire hine bestele, ⁊ hine mon geahsige, fare þær he ær wæs ⁊ geselle his hlaforde LX scill.
Si quis discedat a domino suo sine licentia uel in alium comitatum se furetur, et (deinceps) inueniatur postea, redeat illuc, ubi antea fuit, et emendet domino suo LX sol.
[{LXXXIII}] Gif hwa fare unáliefed fram his hlaforde oððe on oðre scire hine bestele, ⁊ hine mon geahsige, fare þær he ær wæs ⁊ geselle his hlaforde LX sciƚƚ.
If someone moves away from his lord without permission or steals away into another shire, and he is found, let him return to where he was before and let him pay his lord 60 shillings.
If anyone moves away without permission from his lord and steals into another district, if he is discovered he shall return to where he was before, and give his lord 60 shillings.
If anyone goes away from his lord without permission, or steals into another “shire”, and is discovered there, he is to return to where he was before and pay 60 shillings to his lord.

Wenn jemand von seinem Herrn ohne Erlaubniss fortzieht oder sich in einen anderen Amtsbezirk fortstiehlt, und man ihn erkundet, so ziehe er [dorthin zurück], wo er früher war, und gebe seinem Herrn 60 Schill.
If someone goes away from his lord without permission or steals away into another district, and he is discovered, let him go [back] to where he was before and give his lord 60 shillings.
div.note: In the early laws it is uncertain whether “shire” already bears its later definite meaning, or is used more generally of “jurisdiction”, or “district under one’s jurisdiction”.
